title: Necessity of the WBP common-dual condition
summary: For odd-prime vectorial bent functions, decide whether WBP preimage partitions force the common-sign and common-dual-term condition of Theorem 4.

formal_statement.body: Let $p$ be odd, $n$ be even, $2\le m\le n/2$, and $F:V_n^{(p)}\to V_m^{(p)}$ be vectorial bent. For $c\ne0$, write $F_c(x)=\langle c,F(x)\rangle$. Assume the nonzero components are all regular or all weakly regular but nonregular, and the preimage partition of $F$ belongs to WBP. Must there be one sign $\varepsilon$ and functions $G:V_n^{(p)}\to V_m^{(p)}$ and $h:V_n^{(p)}\to\mathbb F_p$ such that every $F_c$ has sign $\varepsilon$ and $(F_c)^*(x)=\langle c,G(x)\rangle+h(x)$ for all $c\ne0$ and all $x$?

scope.domain: Vectorial bent functions and weakly regular bent preimage partitions
assumptions: n is even and 2 <= m <= n/2
The preimage partition belongs to WBP
All nonzero components are regular or all are weakly regular but nonregular
scope.unresolved_remainder: The binary case and odd-prime scalar case are already settled. arXiv:2606.27776 proves necessity for the strict symmetric subclass with K >= 5 and -A_i = A_i. The remaining odd-prime vectorial WBP partitions without that symmetry are unresolved.

progress.summary: The source proves sufficiency, records necessity in the binary and odd-prime scalar cases, and asks for the remaining odd-prime vectorial converse.

progress.summary: A later preprint proves the common-dual characterization with h = 0 for symmetric odd-prime bent partitions, leaving the general WBP converse open.
